While writing the name, substituents are arranged in alphabetical order. 'Ethyl' comes before 'methyl' (ignoring the prefix 'di').

Thus, the correct IUPAC name is 5-Ethyl-3,3-dimethylheptane.

A dichloro organic compound is known to contain exactly two chlorine atoms per molecule. When $0.075 \text{ g}$ of this compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate in a Carius tube, it produces $0.1435 \text{ g}$ of silver chloride $(\text{AgCl})$ precipitate. The molar mass of the organic compound is $\ldots\ldots \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
(Given: Atomic masses of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ u}$ and $\text{Cl} = 35.5 \text{ u}$)
questions.question:
A dichloro organic compound is known to contain exactly two chlorine atoms per molecule. When $0.075 \text{ g}$ of this compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate in a Carius tube, it produces $0.1435 \text{ g}$ of silver chloride $(\text{AgCl})$ precipitate. The molar mass of the organic compound is $\ldots\ldots \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
(Given: Atomic masses of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ u}$ and $\text{Cl} = 35.5 \text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{AgCl} = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of $\text{AgCl}$ formed $= \dfrac{0.1435}{143.5} = 0.001 \text{ mol}$

Moles of chlorine atoms in the sample $= 0.001 \text{ mol}$

Since each molecule of the organic compound contains $2$ chlorine atoms, the moles of the organic compound will be half the moles of chlorine atoms.

Moles of organic compound $= \dfrac{0.001}{2} = 0.0005 \text{ mol}$

Molar mass of the compound $= \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Moles}} = \dfrac{0.075}{0.0005} = 150 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $150$

questions.question: Which of the following diketones has all its carbon atoms $sp^2$ hybridized and forms a continuous conjugated system?
questions.solution:
To determine the correct molecule, we must check both for conjugation and the hybridization of every carbon atom.

Hex-3-ene-2,5-dione: $CH_3-C(=O)-CH=CH-C(=O)-CH_3$. While the central core is conjugated, the two terminal methyl ($CH_3$) groups contain $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms.

Cyclohex-2-ene-1,4-dione: Contains a conjugated system involving one $C=C$ bond and two $C=O$ bonds, but the ring also contains two $sp^3$ hybridized $CH_2$ groups at positions 5 and 6.

Cyclopent-4-ene-1,3-dione: Contains a $C=C$ bond and two $C=O$ bonds. The carbon atom at position 2 is a $CH_2$ group, which is $sp^3$ hybridized and breaks the continuous conjugation.

Cyclohexa-2,5-diene-1,4-dione: A six-membered ring with two $C=O$ bonds at positions 1 and 4, and two $C=C$ bonds at positions 2 and 5. Every carbon atom in the ring is involved in a double bond, meaning all six carbon atoms are $sp^2$ hybridized and form a single continuous conjugated system.

Answer: Cyclohexa-2,5-diene-1,4-dione

questions.q: In an analysis of an organic compound using Kjeldahl's method, the compound is found to contain $42\%$ nitrogen by mass. If $0.5\text{ g}$ of this compound is subjected to the procedure, the evolved ammonia completely neutralizes a certain volume of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution. The volume of the acid consumed is _____ $\text{mL}$.
questions.question: In an analysis of an organic compound using Kjeldahl's method, the compound is found to contain $42\%$ nitrogen by mass. If $0.5\text{ g}$ of this compound is subjected to the procedure, the evolved ammonia completely neutralizes a certain volume of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution. The volume of the acid consumed is _____ $\text{mL}$.
questions.solution:
According to Kjeldahl's method, the percentage of nitrogen is given by:

$\%\text{N} = \dfrac{1.4 \times N \times V}{w}$

where $N$ is the normality of the acid, $V$ is the volume of the acid in $\text{mL}$, and $w$ is the mass of the organic compound.

Given:
$\%\text{N} = 42$
$w = 0.5\text{ g}$
Molarity of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 0.5\text{ M}$

The n-factor for $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $2$.
Normality of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1.0\text{ N}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$42 = \dfrac{1.4 \times 1.0 \times V}{0.5}$

$V = \dfrac{42 \times 0.5}{1.4} = \dfrac{21}{1.4} = 15\text{ mL}$

Answer: $15$

questions.q:
Consider the following reactions that generate major organic ionic species P, Q, R, and S:
I. Cyclopentadiene + $\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{P}$ (organic anion)
II. 3-Bromocyclopropene + $\text{AgSbF}_6 \rightarrow \text{Q}$ (organic cation)
III. Cyclooctatetraene + $2\text{K} \rightarrow \text{R}$ (organic dianion)
IV. 5-Bromo-1,3-cyclopentadiene + $\text{AgSbF}_6 \rightarrow \text{S}$ (organic cation)

Which of the species P, Q, R, and S are aromatic?
questions.question:
Consider the following reactions that generate major organic ionic species P, Q, R, and S:
I. Cyclopentadiene + $\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{P}$ (organic anion)
II. 3-Bromocyclopropene + $\text{AgSbF}_6 \rightarrow \text{Q}$ (organic cation)
III. Cyclooctatetraene + $2\text{K} \rightarrow \text{R}$ (organic dianion)
IV. 5-Bromo-1,3-cyclopentadiene + $\text{AgSbF}_6 \rightarrow \text{S}$ (organic cation)

Which of the species P, Q, R, and S are aromatic?
questions.solution:
Let us analyze the organic ionic species formed in each reaction:

Reaction I: Cyclopentadiene reacts with sodium metal to form the cyclopentadienyl anion (P). This anion is planar, completely conjugated, and has $6\pi$-electrons. It follows Hückel's $(4n+2)$ rule ($n=1$) and is aromatic.

Reaction II: 3-Bromocyclopropene reacts with $\text{AgSbF}_6$ to undergo halide abstraction, forming the cyclopropenyl cation (Q). This cation is planar, completely conjugated, and has $2\pi$-electrons. It follows Hückel's rule ($n=0$) and is aromatic.

Reaction III: Cyclooctatetraene reacts with potassium metal to accept two electrons, forming the cyclooctatetraenyl dianion (R). The addition of two electrons flattens the tub-shaped ring, creating a planar, completely conjugated system with $10\pi$-electrons. It follows Hückel's rule ($n=2$) and is aromatic.

Reaction IV: 5-Bromo-1,3-cyclopentadiene reacts with $\text{AgSbF}_6$ to form the cyclopentadienyl cation (S). This cation is planar and completely conjugated but has $4\pi$-electrons. It follows the $4n$ rule ($n=1$) and is anti-aromatic.

Therefore, only P, Q, and R are aromatic.

Answer: P, Q and R only
questions.explanation:
Let us analyze the organic ionic species formed in each reaction:

Reaction I: Cyclopentadiene reacts with sodium metal to form the cyclopentadienyl anion (P). This anion is planar, completely conjugated, and has $6\pi$-electrons. It follows Hückel's $(4n+2)$ rule ($n=1$) and is aromatic.

Reaction II: 3-Bromocyclopropene reacts with $\text{AgSbF}_6$ to undergo halide abstraction, forming the cyclopropenyl cation (Q). This cation is planar, completely conjugated, and has $2\pi$-electrons. It follows Hückel's rule ($n=0$) and is aromatic.

Reaction III: Cyclooctatetraene reacts with potassium metal to accept two electrons, forming the cyclooctatetraenyl dianion (R). The addition of two electrons flattens the tub-shaped ring, creating a planar, completely conjugated system with $10\pi$-electrons. It follows Hückel's rule ($n=2$) and is aromatic.

Reaction IV: 5-Bromo-1,3-cyclopentadiene reacts with $\text{AgSbF}_6$ to form the cyclopentadienyl cation (S). This cation is planar and completely conjugated but has $4\pi$-electrons. It follows the $4n$ rule ($n=1$) and is anti-aromatic.

Therefore, only P, Q, and R are aromatic.

Answer: P, Q and R only

questions.q: The addition of $\text{HCl}$ to an unknown alkene of molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ yields $2$-chloro-$2,3$-dimethylbutane as the major product. The total number of structurally isomeric alkenes of formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ that can produce this compound as the major product is.........
questions.question: The addition of $\text{HCl}$ to an unknown alkene of molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ yields $2$-chloro-$2,3$-dimethylbutane as the major product. The total number of structurally isomeric alkenes of formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ that can produce this compound as the major product is.........
questions.solution:
The major product, $2$-chloro-$2,3$-dimethylbutane, is formed via the most stable carbocation intermediate, which is the tertiary $2,3$-dimethyl-$2$-butyl cation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

We must identify all structurally isomeric alkenes of formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ that form this specific carbocation (either directly or via rearrangement) as their most stable intermediate.

Direct protonation yields this cation from two alkenes:
$1$. $2,3$-dimethyl-$2$-butene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$)
$2$. $2,3$-dimethyl-$1$-butene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$)

Protonation followed by a $1,2$-methyl shift yields this cation from one alkene:
$3$. $3,3$-dimethyl-$1$-butene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$).
Its initial protonation gives a secondary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+\text{H}-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$), which undergoes a $1,2$-methyl shift to form the more stable tertiary $2,3$-dimethyl-$2$-butyl cation.

No other structural isomers of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ will form this specific tertiary carbocation as their most stable intermediate. Thus, there are exactly $3$ such structurally isomeric alkenes.

Answer: $3$

In the Dumas method for the estimation of nitrogen, $0.28\text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave $89.6\text{ mL}$ of nitrogen gas collected over water at $273\text{ K}$ and a total pressure of $400\text{ mm Hg}$. If the aqueous tension at $273\text{ K}$ is $20\text{ mm Hg}$, the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ________.

(Given: Molar mass of $\text{N}_2$ is $28\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, Molar volume of $\text{N}_2$ at STP is $22400\text{ mL}$, Standard pressure is $760\text{ mm Hg}$)
questions.question:
In the Dumas method for the estimation of nitrogen, $0.28\text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave $89.6\text{ mL}$ of nitrogen gas collected over water at $273\text{ K}$ and a total pressure of $400\text{ mm Hg}$. If the aqueous tension at $273\text{ K}$ is $20\text{ mm Hg}$, the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ________.

(Given: Molar mass of $\text{N}_2$ is $28\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, Molar volume of $\text{N}_2$ at STP is $22400\text{ mL}$, Standard pressure is $760\text{ mm Hg}$)
questions.solution:
Pressure of dry $\text{N}_2$ gas:
$P_{\text{dry}} = P_{\text{total}} - \text{Aqueous tension} = 400 - 20 = 380\text{ mm Hg}$

Since the temperature is $273\text{ K}$ (which is standard temperature), we apply Boyle's Law to find the volume at standard pressure ($760\text{ mm Hg}$):
$V_{\text{STP}} = \dfrac{P_{\text{dry}} \times V_{\text{obs}}}{760} = \dfrac{380 \times 89.6}{760} = 44.8\text{ mL}$

Moles of $\text{N}_2$ gas at STP:
$n = \dfrac{44.8}{22400} = 0.002\text{ mol}$

Mass of $\text{N}_2$ gas:
$W = 0.002 \times 28 = 0.056\text{ g}$

Percentage of nitrogen in the compound:
$\%\text{ N} = \dfrac{0.056}{0.28} \times 100 = 20\%$

Answer: $20$

questions.q: An organic compound is separated using Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) on a glass plate coated with silica gel. If the distance travelled by the solvent front is $10 \text{ cm}$ and the distance travelled by the compound spot is $4 \text{ cm}$, what is the fundamental principle involved in this separation and the retardation factor ($R_f$) of the compound?
questions.question: An organic compound is separated using Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) on a glass plate coated with silica gel. If the distance travelled by the solvent front is $10 \text{ cm}$ and the distance travelled by the compound spot is $4 \text{ cm}$, what is the fundamental principle involved in this separation and the retardation factor ($R_f$) of the compound?
questions.solution:
Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) is a type of adsorption chromatography where a thin layer of a solid like silica gel or alumina acts as the stationary phase (adsorbent).

The retardation factor ($R_f$) is calculated as:
$R_f = \dfrac{\text{Distance travelled by the compound}}{\text{Distance travelled by the solvent front}}$

Given:
Distance travelled by the compound = $4 \text{ cm}$
Distance travelled by the solvent front = $10 \text{ cm}$

$R_f = \dfrac{4}{10} = 0.4$

Therefore, the principle is adsorption chromatography and the $R_f$ value is $0.4$.

Answer: Adsorption chromatography, $0.4$

Consider the following compounds:
I. Cyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one
II. Pentane-2,4-dione
III. Ethyl 3-oxobutanoate
IV. Propan-2-one

The correct decreasing order of their enol content is:
questions.question:
Consider the following compounds:
I. Cyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one
II. Pentane-2,4-dione
III. Ethyl 3-oxobutanoate
IV. Propan-2-one

The correct decreasing order of their enol content is:
questions.solution:
The enol content of a compound depends on the thermodynamic stability of its enol form relative to its keto form.

Compound I (Cyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one) tautomerizes to phenol. The resulting enol form is aromatic, which provides exceptional thermodynamic stability. Its enol content is nearly $100\%$.

Compound II (Pentane-2,4-dione) is a $\beta$-diketone. Its enol form is stabilized by extended conjugation and strong intramolecular hydrogen bonding, forming a stable six-membered chelate ring. Its enol content is significant (around $76\%$).

Compound III (Ethyl 3-oxobutanoate) is a $\beta$-keto ester. The cross-conjugation from the ester oxygen lone pair reduces the electron-withdrawing ability of the ester carbonyl. This weakens the intramolecular hydrogen bond compared to a $\beta$-diketone, leading to a lower enol content (around $8\%$).

Compound IV (Propan-2-one) is a simple ketone. Its enol form lacks any special stabilization such as extended conjugation or intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so its enol content is negligible (around $10^{-5}\%$).

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of enol content is I > II > III > IV.

Answer: I > II > III > IV

questions.q:
Consider the following acid-base equilibrium reactions:
(A) Phenol + Sodium ethoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium phenoxide + Ethanol
(B) p-Nitrophenol + Sodium phenoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium p-nitrophenoxide + Phenol
(C) tert-Butanol + Sodium methoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium tert-butoxide + Methanol
(D) p-Cresol + Sodium phenoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium p-cresolate + Phenol

Which of the above reactions proceed predominantly in the forward direction?
questions.question:
Consider the following acid-base equilibrium reactions:
(A) Phenol + Sodium ethoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium phenoxide + Ethanol
(B) p-Nitrophenol + Sodium phenoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium p-nitrophenoxide + Phenol
(C) tert-Butanol + Sodium methoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium tert-butoxide + Methanol
(D) p-Cresol + Sodium phenoxide $\rightleftharpoons$ Sodium p-cresolate + Phenol

Which of the above reactions proceed predominantly in the forward direction?
questions.solution:
An acid-base reaction $HA + B^- \rightleftharpoons A^- + HB$ proceeds predominantly in the forward direction if the reactant acid ($HA$) is stronger than the product acid ($HB$).

In reaction (A), the reactant acid is phenol and the product acid is ethanol. Since phenols are more acidic than aliphatic alcohols, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction.

In reaction (B), the reactant acid is p-nitrophenol and the product acid is phenol. The $-NO_2$ group is electron-withdrawing ($-I, -M$), making p-nitrophenol a stronger acid than phenol. The reaction proceeds in the forward direction.

In reaction (C), the reactant acid is tert-butanol and the product acid is methanol. Due to the $+I$ effect of three methyl groups, tert-butanol is a weaker acid than methanol. The reaction proceeds in the backward direction.

In reaction (D), the reactant acid is p-cresol and the product acid is phenol. The $-CH_3$ group is electron-donating ($+I$, hyperconjugation), making p-cresol a weaker acid than phenol. The reaction proceeds in the backward direction.

Therefore, only reactions (A) and (B) proceed predominantly in the forward direction.

Answer: (A) and (B) only

Consider the following pairs of organic compounds:
(I) o-Cresol and Benzyl alcohol
(II) Propan-1-amine and N-methylethanamine
(III) Butanoic acid and Methyl propanoate
(IV) Pentan-2-one and Pentan-3-one
(V) Propanal and Butanone

The number of pairs that represent functional isomers is:
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of organic compounds:
(I) o-Cresol and Benzyl alcohol
(II) Propan-1-amine and N-methylethanamine
(III) Butanoic acid and Methyl propanoate
(IV) Pentan-2-one and Pentan-3-one
(V) Propanal and Butanone

The number of pairs that represent functional isomers is:
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each pair to determine if they are functional isomers. Functional isomers must have the exact same molecular formula but different functional groups.

(I) o-Cresol is a phenol ($-OH$ attached directly to the benzene ring), while Benzyl alcohol is an alcohol ($-OH$ attached to an $sp^3$ carbon). Both have the molecular formula $C_7H_8O$. They are functional isomers.

(II) Propan-1-amine is a $1^{\circ}$ amine, and N-methylethanamine is a $2^{\circ}$ amine. Both have the molecular formula $C_3H_9N$. Amines of different degrees are considered functional isomers.

(III) Butanoic acid is a carboxylic acid, and Methyl propanoate is an ester. Both have the molecular formula $C_4H_8O_2$. They are functional isomers.

(IV) Pentan-2-one and Pentan-3-one are both ketones with the molecular formula $C_5H_{10}O$. Since their functional group is the same, they are position isomers (or metamers), not functional isomers.

(V) Propanal has the molecular formula $C_3H_6O$, whereas Butanone has the molecular formula $C_4H_8O$. Since their molecular formulas are different, they are not isomers at all.

Therefore, only pairs (I), (II), and (III) are functional isomers. The total number of correct pairs is 3.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Four Newman projections of 2,3-butanediol, viewed down the C2-C3 bond, are described below. The positions of the groups on the front and back carbons are given by their clock-face angles (where 0° is straight up, 120° is bottom-right, 240° is bottom-left, etc.). Which of these represents a meso compound?
questions.question: Four Newman projections of 2,3-butanediol, viewed down the C2-C3 bond, are described below. The positions of the groups on the front and back carbons are given by their clock-face angles (where 0° is straight up, 120° is bottom-right, 240° is bottom-left, etc.). Which of these represents a meso compound?
options:
Front carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°
Back carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 180°, $-\text{H}$ at 300°, $-\text{OH}$ at 60°

Front carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°
Back carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 180°, $-\text{OH}$ at 300°, $-\text{H}$ at 60°

Front carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°
Back carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{H}$ at 120°, $-\text{OH}$ at 240°

Front carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°
Back carbon: $-\text{OH}$ at 180°, $-\text{CH}_3$ at 300°, $-\text{H}$ at 60°
questions.solution:
To identify the meso compound from a Newman projection, we can look for a conformation that possesses a center of inversion or a plane of symmetry, or we can convert it to a Fischer projection to check for an internal plane of symmetry.

A staggered Newman projection has a center of inversion if every group on the front carbon at an angle $\theta$ is identical to the group on the back carbon at an angle $\theta + 180^\circ$.

Let us analyze Option 2:
Front carbon groups: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°.
Back carbon groups: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 180°, $-\text{OH}$ at 300°, $-\text{H}$ at 60°.
Comparing the positions:
Front $-\text{CH}_3$ (0°) $\rightarrow$ Back $-\text{CH}_3$ (180°)
Front $-\text{OH}$ (120°) $\rightarrow$ Back $-\text{OH}$ (120° + 180° = 300°)
Front $-\text{H}$ (240°) $\rightarrow$ Back $-\text{H}$ (240° + 180° = 420° $\equiv$ 60°)
Since all groups match perfectly through the center of the C2-C3 bond, this conformation possesses a center of inversion. Therefore, the molecule is achiral and represents the meso isomer.

Alternatively, rotating the back carbon by 180° to form the eclipsed conformation gives $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, and $-\text{H}$ at 240° for both carbons. This perfectly eclipsed conformation has a plane of symmetry perpendicular to the C-C bond, confirming it is meso.

The other options lack this symmetry and represent the optically active (2S,3S) or (2R,3R) enantiomers.

Answer: Front carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°
Back carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 180°, $-\text{OH}$ at 300°, $-\text{H}$ at 60°
questions.explanation:
To identify the meso compound from a Newman projection, we can look for a conformation that possesses a center of inversion or a plane of symmetry, or we can convert it to a Fischer projection to check for an internal plane of symmetry.

A staggered Newman projection has a center of inversion if every group on the front carbon at an angle $\theta$ is identical to the group on the back carbon at an angle $\theta + 180^\circ$.

Let us analyze Option 2:
Front carbon groups: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°.
Back carbon groups: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 180°, $-\text{OH}$ at 300°, $-\text{H}$ at 60°.
Comparing the positions:
Front $-\text{CH}_3$ (0°) $\rightarrow$ Back $-\text{CH}_3$ (180°)
Front $-\text{OH}$ (120°) $\rightarrow$ Back $-\text{OH}$ (120° + 180° = 300°)
Front $-\text{H}$ (240°) $\rightarrow$ Back $-\text{H}$ (240° + 180° = 420° $\equiv$ 60°)
Since all groups match perfectly through the center of the C2-C3 bond, this conformation possesses a center of inversion. Therefore, the molecule is achiral and represents the meso isomer.

Alternatively, rotating the back carbon by 180° to form the eclipsed conformation gives $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, and $-\text{H}$ at 240° for both carbons. This perfectly eclipsed conformation has a plane of symmetry perpendicular to the C-C bond, confirming it is meso.

The other options lack this symmetry and represent the optically active (2S,3S) or (2R,3R) enantiomers.

Answer: Front carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 0°, $-\text{OH}$ at 120°, $-\text{H}$ at 240°
Back carbon: $-\text{CH}_3$ at 180°, $-\text{OH}$ at 300°, $-\text{H}$ at 60°

In the Carius method, $150 \text{ mg}$ of a dichlorinated organic compound (containing exactly two chlorine atoms per molecule) yields $287 \text{ mg}$ of $\mathrm{AgCl}$. The molar mass of the organic compound is _______ $\mathrm{g \ mol}^{-1}$.
(Given : molar mass in $\mathrm{g \ mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{Ag} : 108, \mathrm{Cl} : 35.5$)
questions.question:
In the Carius method, $150 \text{ mg}$ of a dichlorinated organic compound (containing exactly two chlorine atoms per molecule) yields $287 \text{ mg}$ of $\mathrm{AgCl}$. The molar mass of the organic compound is _______ $\mathrm{g \ mol}^{-1}$.
(Given : molar mass in $\mathrm{g \ mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{Ag} : 108, \mathrm{Cl} : 35.5$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgCl} = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ formed $= \dfrac{287 \times 10^{-3}}{143.5} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$.

Since 1 mole of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ contains 1 mole of $\mathrm{Cl}$, the moles of chlorine atoms $= 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$.

The organic compound contains exactly 2 chlorine atoms per molecule. Therefore, moles of the organic compound $= \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-3}}{2} = 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$.

Molar mass of the compound $= \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Moles}} = \dfrac{150 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g}}{10^{-3} \text{ mol}} = 150 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $150$

questions.solution:
(I) 3-bromo-3-methylpentane: The C3 atom is bonded to a methyl group, a bromine atom, and two identical ethyl groups. It is achiral.

(III) 1,4-dichlorocyclohexane: The paths around the ring from C1 to C4 are identical. It is achiral.

(IV) 1,3-dichlorocyclopentane: The C1 atom is bonded to $-\text{H}$, $-\text{Cl}$, and two different paths around the ring ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})-$ and $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-$). It is chiral.

(V) 2,3-dimethylbutane: The C2 atom is bonded to two identical methyl groups. It is achiral.

(VI) 1-chloro-2-methylbutane: The C2 atom is bonded to $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, and $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is chiral.

Therefore, compounds (II), (IV), and (VI) contain chiral carbon atoms. Total count is 3.

Answer: $3$

questions.q: An organic compound 'A' is heated with fuming nitric acid in a Carius tube. The resulting acid is treated with magnesia mixture to yield a precipitate, which on ignition forms a stable pyrophosphate compound. The compound 'A' could be:
questions.question: An organic compound 'A' is heated with fuming nitric acid in a Carius tube. The resulting acid is treated with magnesia mixture to yield a precipitate, which on ignition forms a stable pyrophosphate compound. The compound 'A' could be:
questions.solution:
Heating an organic compound with fuming nitric acid oxidizes the phosphorus present in it to phosphoric acid. On adding magnesia mixture, a precipitate of magnesium ammonium phosphate is formed, which on ignition yields magnesium pyrophosphate ($\text{Mg}_2\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$). This is the standard test for the estimation of phosphorus.

Among the given options, a nucleotide contains a phosphate group and hence contains phosphorus. Cysteine contains sulphur, chloramphenicol contains chlorine, and thyroxine contains iodine.

Answer: A nucleotide

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $2$-Hydroxy-$3$-phenylpropanoic acid has a degree of unsaturation of $5$, contains exactly one chiral carbon atom, and dissolves in aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution.
Statement II: Penta-$2,3$-diene is a non-planar molecule containing exactly two $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atoms and one $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized carbon atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $2$-Hydroxy-$3$-phenylpropanoic acid has a degree of unsaturation of $5$, contains exactly one chiral carbon atom, and dissolves in aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution.
Statement II: Penta-$2,3$-diene is a non-planar molecule containing exactly two $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atoms and one $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized carbon atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Statement I: The structure of $2$-hydroxy-$3$-phenylpropanoic acid is $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-CH(OH)-COOH}$.
Degree of unsaturation (DU) = $4$ (for the phenyl ring) + $1$ (for the $\mathrm{C=O}$ in $-\mathrm{COOH}$) = $5$.
It contains exactly one chiral center at the $\mathrm{C-2}$ position, which is attached to four different groups: $-\mathrm{H}$, $-\mathrm{OH}$, $-\mathrm{COOH}$, and $-\mathrm{CH_2C_6H_5}$.
Due to the presence of the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group, it dissolves in aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ with effervescence. Thus, Statement I is true.

Statement II: The structure of penta-$2,3$-diene is $\mathrm{CH_3-CH=C=CH-CH_3}$.
The central carbon ($\mathrm{C-3}$) is $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized, while the adjacent carbons ($\mathrm{C-2}$ and $\mathrm{C-4}$) are $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized. Thus, it contains exactly two $\mathrm{sp^2}$ carbons and one $\mathrm{sp}$ carbon.
Because it is an allene with an even number of cumulated double bonds, the $\pi$-bonds are orthogonal to each other. This forces the terminal $-\mathrm{H}$ and $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ groups to lie in perpendicular planes, making the molecule non-planar. Thus, Statement II is true.

Both statements are true.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

Which of the following statements regarding the separation and purification of organic compounds are correct?
A. In column chromatography, a solid such as alumina or silica gel is used as the stationary phase.
B. The $R_f$ (retardation factor) value in thin layer chromatography can be greater than 1.
C. Paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography in which water trapped in the paper acts as the stationary phase.
D. Differential extraction separates components based on their different boiling points.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the separation and purification of organic compounds are correct?
A. In column chromatography, a solid such as alumina or silica gel is used as the stationary phase.
B. The $R_f$ (retardation factor) value in thin layer chromatography can be greater than 1.
C. Paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography in which water trapped in the paper acts as the stationary phase.
D. Differential extraction separates components based on their different boiling points.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: In column chromatography, a solid adsorbent like alumina or silica gel acts as the stationary phase.

Statement B is incorrect: The $R_f$ value is the ratio of the distance moved by the substance to the distance moved by the solvent front. Since the substance cannot move further than the solvent front, the $R_f$ value is always less than or equal to 1.

Statement C is correct: Paper chromatography is a form of partition chromatography where the water trapped within the cellulose network of the paper acts as the stationary phase.

Statement D is incorrect: Differential extraction is based on the difference in solubilities of a compound in two immiscible liquids (usually water and an organic solvent), not on their boiling points.

Answer: A and C only

questions.question:

(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Ba} = 137 \text{ u}, \text{S} = 32 \text{ u}, \text{O} = 16 \text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 233 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of $\text{BaSO}_4$ formed:

Since one mole of $\text{BaSO}_4$ contains one mole of sulphur atoms, the moles of sulphur in the sample is $0.006 \text{ mol}$.

The number of sulphur atoms per molecule of the compound is the ratio of moles of sulphur to moles of the compound:
$\text{Number of S atoms} = \dfrac{0.006}{0.002} = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is non-aromatic in nature?
questions.question: Which of the following compounds is non-aromatic in nature?
questions.solution:
According to Huckel's rule, a planar, fully conjugated cyclic system with $(4n+2)\pi$ electrons is aromatic, while one with $4n\pi$ electrons is anti-aromatic.

Azulene is a fused bicyclic system with $10\pi$ electrons ($n=2$). It is planar and aromatic.

Pyrrole is a five-membered heterocycle. The lone pair on the nitrogen atom participates in conjugation, giving $6\pi$ electrons ($n=1$). It is planar and aromatic.

Cyclopropenyl cation has $2\pi$ electrons ($n=0$) in a continuous cyclic array of p-orbitals. It is planar and aromatic.

Cyclooctatetraene has $8\pi$ electrons ($4n$, where $n=2$). If it were planar, it would be highly unstable and anti-aromatic. To relieve angle strain and avoid anti-aromatic destabilization, it adopts a non-planar 'tub' conformation. This breaks the continuous cyclic conjugation, making the molecule non-aromatic.

Answer: Cyclooctatetraene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Pairs of compounds)List II (Types of isomerism)
A. Ethoxyethane and 1-MethoxypropaneI. Chain isomerism
B. Pentan-1-ol and 3-Methylbutan-1-olII. Position isomerism
C. Butanal and Butan-2-oneIII. Functional isomerism
D. Butan-1-amine and Butan-2-amineIV. Metamerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Let us analyze each pair of compounds:

A. Ethoxyethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and 1-Methoxypropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) have the same molecular formula ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) and the same polyvalent functional group (ether) but differ in the alkyl groups attached to the oxygen atom. This is an example of metamerism. (A $\rightarrow$ IV)

B. Pentan-1-ol and 3-Methylbutan-1-ol have the same molecular formula ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$) and the same functional group ($-\text{OH}$) at the same position, but they differ in the length of the principal carbon chain (5 carbons vs 4 carbons). This is an example of chain isomerism. (B $\rightarrow$ I)

C. Butanal is an aldehyde and Butan-2-one is a ketone. They have the same molecular formula ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$) but different functional groups. This is an example of functional isomerism. (C $\rightarrow$ III)

D. Butan-1-amine and Butan-2-amine have the same molecular formula ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$) and the same principal carbon chain. The primary amine group ($-\text{NH}_2$) is attached at the 1st carbon in the former and the 2nd carbon in the latter. Since $-\text{NH}_2$ is a monovalent group, this represents position isomerism. (D $\rightarrow$ II)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds has the lowest enol content?
questions.question: Which of the following compounds has the lowest enol content?
questions.solution:
The enol content in $\beta$-dicarbonyl compounds is typically very high due to the formation of a stable, six-membered, intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded ring and extended conjugation. This stabilization requires the presence of at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom on the active methylene group situated between the two carbonyl groups.

In 3,3-dimethylpentane-2,4-dione, the carbon atom between the two carbonyl groups is bonded to two methyl groups and has no hydrogen atoms. Because the active methylene position is blocked, it cannot form the highly stable conjugated enol system. Enolization can only occur at the terminal methyl groups, which yields a simple, isolated enol without the strong stabilization of a chelated ring. Thus, its enol content is the lowest.

Pentane-2,4-dione, 3-oxobutanal, and 1,3-diphenylpropane-1,3-dione all possess active methylene hydrogens and readily form highly stabilized, conjugated enols.

Answer: 3,3-Dimethylpentane-2,4-dione

questions.question: Consider the two isomeric products formed when phenol reacts with dilute nitric acid at $298\text{ K}$. Which of the following statements regarding the physical properties and separation of these isomers is INCORRECT?
options: The mixture of these isomers can be efficiently separated by steam distillation.
$o$-nitrophenol is more soluble in water than $p$-nitrophenol.
$o$-nitrophenol has a lower boiling point than $p$-nitrophenol.
$p$-nitrophenol is less volatile in steam due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
questions.solution:
The reaction of phenol with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ at $298\text{ K}$ yields $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol.

$o$-nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation). This prevents the molecules from associating with each other, resulting in a lower boiling point and making it steam volatile. Furthermore, because its polar groups are involved in internal hydrogen bonding, they are less available to form hydrogen bonds with water, making $o$-nitrophenol less soluble in water.

$p$-nitrophenol exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding. This causes molecular association, leading to a higher boiling point and making it non-volatile in steam. However, it can readily form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making it more soluble in water than the ortho isomer.

Therefore, the statement claiming $o$-nitrophenol is more soluble in water than $p$-nitrophenol is incorrect.

Answer: $o$-nitrophenol is more soluble in water than $p$-nitrophenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unknown organic compound 'X' is subjected to quantitative analysis for nitrogen. It successfully yields nitrogen gas when analysed by Dumas method, but fails to yield ammonia when subjected to Kjeldahl's method.

Identify compound 'X' from the given options.
questions.question:
An unknown organic compound 'X' is subjected to quantitative analysis for nitrogen. It successfully yields nitrogen gas when analysed by Dumas method, but fails to yield ammonia when subjected to Kjeldahl's method.

Identify compound 'X' from the given options.
questions.solution:
Dumas method is universally applicable for the estimation of nitrogen in all types of nitrogen-containing organic compounds.

Kjeldahl's method has limitations: it is not applicable to compounds containing nitrogen in nitro groups, azo groups, and nitrogen present in the ring.

Azobenzene contains an azo group ($-N=N-$), so its nitrogen cannot be converted to ammonium sulphate in Kjeldahl's method, thus failing to yield ammonia.

Benzylamine, N-Methylaniline, and Acetamide contain amine or amide nitrogen, which successfully undergo Kjeldahl digestion to yield ammonia. Therefore, compound 'X' is Azobenzene.

Answer: Azobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When $(3E)-1,3$-pentadiene is reacted with one equivalent of $\text{HBr}$ at $40^\circ\text{C}$, a major structural product is formed under thermodynamic control. The total number of stereoisomers of this major product is.........
questions.question: When $(3E)-1,3$-pentadiene is reacted with one equivalent of $\text{HBr}$ at $40^\circ\text{C}$, a major structural product is formed under thermodynamic control. The total number of stereoisomers of this major product is.........
questions.solution:
Protonation of $1,3$-pentadiene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$) occurs at C1 to form the more stable secondary allylic carbocation, which is resonance stabilized:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+\text{H}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}^+\text{H}-\text{CH}_3$

At $40^\circ\text{C}$, the reaction is under thermodynamic control, yielding the most stable alkene (most substituted). Attack of the bromide ion at either C2 or C4 of the resonance-stabilized carbocation yields the same disubstituted alkene: $4$-bromo-$2$-pentene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$).

The molecule $4$-bromo-$2$-pentene has one double bond capable of exhibiting geometrical isomerism (E/Z) and one chiral center (C4) capable of exhibiting optical isomerism (R/S).
Since the two ends of the molecule are different, there is no plane of symmetry.
Total number of stereoisomers $= 2^n = 2^2 = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
(A) Biphenyl(I) Non-benzenoid aromatic
(B) Tropylium cation(II) Benzenoid aromatic
(C) Cyclooctatetraene(III) Anti-aromatic
(D) Cyclopropenyl anion(IV) Non-aromatic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
(A) Biphenyl(I) Non-benzenoid aromatic
(B) Tropylium cation(II) Benzenoid aromatic
(C) Cyclooctatetraene(III) Anti-aromatic
(D) Cyclopropenyl anion(IV) Non-aromatic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Biphenyl consists of two connected benzene rings, making it a benzenoid aromatic compound. So, (A) matches with (II).

(B) Tropylium cation is a planar seven-membered ring with $6\pi$ electrons. It satisfies Huckel's rule but lacks a benzene ring, making it a non-benzenoid aromatic compound. So, (B) matches with (I).

(C) Cyclooctatetraene has $8\pi$ electrons ($4n\pi$ system). To avoid anti-aromaticity and relieve angle strain, it adopts a non-planar tub shape, making it non-aromatic. So, (C) matches with (IV).

(D) Cyclopropenyl anion is a planar three-membered ring with $4\pi$ electrons ($2$ from the double bond and $2$ from the negative charge). It satisfies the $4n\pi$ rule, making it anti-aromatic. So, (D) matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkane is represented by a Newman projection looking down a carbon-carbon bond. The front carbon is bonded to two methyl groups and one ethyl group. The back carbon is bonded to one hydrogen atom, one ethyl group, and one n-propyl group. The correct IUPAC name of this alkane is :
questions.question: An alkane is represented by a Newman projection looking down a carbon-carbon bond. The front carbon is bonded to two methyl groups and one ethyl group. The back carbon is bonded to one hydrogen atom, one ethyl group, and one n-propyl group. The correct IUPAC name of this alkane is :
questions.solution:
First, translate the Newman projection into a connectivity diagram.
The front carbon ($C_F$) is bonded to two $-\text{CH}_3$ groups and one $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group.
The back carbon ($C_B$) is bonded to one $-\text{H}$ atom, one $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group, and one $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group.

To find the longest continuous carbon chain, we must trace the longest path through the $C_F-C_B$ bond.
The longest branch attached to $C_F$ is the ethyl group (2 carbons).
The longest branch attached to $C_B$ is the n-propyl group (3 carbons).
The longest chain consists of: 2 carbons (ethyl) + $C_F$ + $C_B$ + 3 carbons (n-propyl) = 7 carbons. Thus, the parent alkane is heptane.

Numbering the chain from the ethyl group on $C_F$ gives $C_F$ as carbon-3 and $C_B$ as carbon-4. The substituents are two methyl groups at C-3 and one ethyl group at C-4, giving the locant set (3, 3, 4).
Numbering from the n-propyl group on $C_B$ would give $C_B$ as carbon-4 and $C_F$ as carbon-5, giving the locant set (4, 5, 5).

By the lowest locant set rule, (3, 3, 4) is preferred over (4, 5, 5).

Arranging the substituents alphabetically ('ethyl' before 'methyl'), the correct IUPAC name is 4-Ethyl-3,3-dimethylheptane.

Answer: 4-Ethyl-3,3-dimethylheptane

questions.q:
Consider a para-substituted benzyl cation (X), $p\text{-G-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CH}_2^+$, and a para-substituted benzyl anion (Y), $p\text{-G-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CH}_2^-$.

Four possible groups are available for the substituent G: $\text{-OCH}_3$, $\text{-NO}_2$, $\text{-CH}_3$, and $\text{-Cl}$.

Which of the following pairs of substituents for G will make intermediate X the most stable, and intermediate Y the most stable, respectively?
questions.question:
Consider a para-substituted benzyl cation (X), $p\text{-G-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CH}_2^+$, and a para-substituted benzyl anion (Y), $p\text{-G-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CH}_2^-$.

Four possible groups are available for the substituent G: $\text{-OCH}_3$, $\text{-NO}_2$, $\text{-CH}_3$, and $\text{-Cl}$.

Which of the following pairs of substituents for G will make intermediate X the most stable, and intermediate Y the most stable, respectively?
questions.solution:
The stability of a carbocation (X) is increased by electron-donating groups (EDG). Among the given groups, $\text{-OCH}_3$ exerts a strong +M (resonance) effect, which stabilizes the positive charge more effectively than the +H effect of $\text{-CH}_3$. Thus, X is most stable when G is $\text{-OCH}_3$.

The stability of a carbanion (Y) is increased by electron-withdrawing groups (EWG). The $\text{-NO}_2$ group exerts a strong -M and -I effect, which delocalizes the negative charge and provides maximum stability. Thus, Y is most stable when G is $\text{-NO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{-OCH}_3$ for X and $\text{-NO}_2$ for Y

Answer: $\text{-OCH}_3$ for X and $\text{-NO}_2$ for Y

questions.q:
Consider the structural and stereoisomers of the compound with the molecular formula $C_4H_{11}N$. Identify the correct statements from the following:
A. It has exactly 4 structural isomers that are primary amines.
B. It has exactly 3 structural isomers that are secondary amines.
C. Its primary, secondary, and tertiary amine isomers are considered functional isomers of each other.
D. None of its isomers exhibit optical isomerism.
E. The tertiary amine isomer is a metamer of the secondary amines.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Consider the structural and stereoisomers of the compound with the molecular formula $C_4H_{11}N$. Identify the correct statements from the following:
A. It has exactly 4 structural isomers that are primary amines.
B. It has exactly 3 structural isomers that are secondary amines.
C. Its primary, secondary, and tertiary amine isomers are considered functional isomers of each other.
D. None of its isomers exhibit optical isomerism.
E. The tertiary amine isomer is a metamer of the secondary amines.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For the molecular formula $C_4H_{11}N$:

Statement A: The primary ($1^{\circ}$) amines are butan-1-amine, butan-2-amine, 2-methylpropan-1-amine, and 2-methylpropan-2-amine. There are exactly 4 structural isomers. (True)

Statement B: The secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amines are N-methylpropan-1-amine, N-methylpropan-2-amine, and N-ethylethanamine. There are exactly 3 structural isomers. (True)

Statement C: Primary, secondary, and tertiary amines have different functional groups ($-NH_2$, $-NH-$, and $-N<$ respectively), so they are functional isomers of each other. (True)

Statement D: Butan-2-amine ($CH_3CH(NH_2)CH_2CH_3$) contains a chiral carbon atom (attached to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-NH_2$, and $-C_2H_5$) and thus exhibits optical isomerism. (False)

Statement E: Metamers must have the same polyvalent functional group. Since secondary and tertiary amines are considered different functional groups, they are functional isomers, not metamers. (False)

Therefore, only statements A, B, and C are correct.

Answer: A, B and C only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following compounds, which one exhibits the maximum enol content?
questions.question: Among the following compounds, which one exhibits the maximum enol content?
questions.solution:
The enol content of $\beta$-dicarbonyl compounds depends on the stability of the enol form, which is enhanced by intramolecular hydrogen bonding and extended conjugation.

In $1,3$-diphenylpropane-$1,3$-dione, the enol form is highly stabilized by strong intramolecular hydrogen bonding and extended conjugation over the two phenyl rings.

In pentane-$2,4$-dione, the enol form is stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding and conjugation, but lacks the extended conjugation provided by the phenyl rings.

In ethyl $3$-oxobutanoate and diethyl propanedioate, the ester oxygen lone pair participates in cross-conjugation with the carbonyl group. This reduces the electron-withdrawing ability of the carbonyl group, leading to a significantly lower enol content compared to $\beta$-diketones.

Thus, $1,3$-diphenylpropane-$1,3$-dione exhibits the maximum enol content.

Answer: $1,3$-Diphenylpropane-$1,3$-dione

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the Carius method for the estimation of sulphur, $0.16 \text{ g}$ of an organic compound yielded $0.233 \text{ g}$ of barium sulphate. What is the minimum molecular mass of the organic compound?
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{S} = 32 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 233 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
In the Carius method for the estimation of sulphur, $0.16 \text{ g}$ of an organic compound yielded $0.233 \text{ g}$ of barium sulphate. What is the minimum molecular mass of the organic compound?
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{S} = 32 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 233 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
First, calculate the mass of sulphur present in the given mass of $\text{BaSO}_4$:
$\text{Mass of S} = \dfrac{32}{233} \times 0.233 = 0.032 \text{ g}$

Next, find the percentage of sulphur in the organic compound:
$\%\text{S} = \dfrac{0.032}{0.16} \times 100 = 20\%$

For the minimum molecular mass, the compound must contain exactly one atom of sulphur per molecule. Therefore, $20\%$ of the minimum molecular mass ($M$) must equal the molar mass of one sulphur atom ($32 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$).

$M \times \dfrac{20}{100} = 32$
$M = \dfrac{32 \times 100}{20} = 160 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $160 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the Carius method for the estimation of sulphur, $0.200 \text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave a precipitate of barium sulphate. If the percentage of sulphur in the compound is $16\%$, the mass of barium sulphate formed is _______ $\text{mg}$.

(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Ba} = 137 \text{ u}, \text{S} = 32 \text{ u}, \text{O} = 16 \text{ u}$)
questions.question:
In the Carius method for the estimation of sulphur, $0.200 \text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave a precipitate of barium sulphate. If the percentage of sulphur in the compound is $16\%$, the mass of barium sulphate formed is _______ $\text{mg}$.

(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Ba} = 137 \text{ u}, \text{S} = 32 \text{ u}, \text{O} = 16 \text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 233 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

The percentage of sulphur is given by the formula:
$\%\text{S} = \dfrac{32}{233} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of BaSO}_4}{\text{Mass of organic compound}} \times 100$

Substituting the given values:
$16 = \dfrac{32}{233} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of BaSO}_4}{0.200} \times 100$

$16 = \dfrac{3200}{233} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of BaSO}_4}{0.200}$

$\text{Mass of BaSO}_4 = \dfrac{16 \times 233 \times 0.200}{3200} = \dfrac{233}{1000} \text{ g}$

$\text{Mass of BaSO}_4 = 0.233 \text{ g} = 233 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $233$
questions.explanation:
Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 233 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

The percentage of sulphur is given by the formula:

Substituting the given values:
$16 = \dfrac{32}{233} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of BaSO}_4}{0.200} \times 100$

$16 = \dfrac{3200}{233} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of BaSO}_4}{0.200}$

$\text{Mass of BaSO}_4 = \dfrac{16 \times 233 \times 0.200}{3200} = \dfrac{233}{1000} \text{ g}$

$\text{Mass of BaSO}_4 = 0.233 \text{ g} = 233 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $233$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aromatic compound $P$ having the molecular formula $C_6H_6O$ reacts with dilute $HNO_3$ to yield two isomers $A$ and $B$. Isomer $A$ is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas isomer $B$ is not steam volatile. Isomer $B$ is treated with aqueous $NaOH$ followed by the addition of ethyl bromide to yield compound $C$. The total number of hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of compound $C$ is
questions.question: An aromatic compound $P$ having the molecular formula $C_6H_6O$ reacts with dilute $HNO_3$ to yield two isomers $A$ and $B$. Isomer $A$ is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas isomer $B$ is not steam volatile. Isomer $B$ is treated with aqueous $NaOH$ followed by the addition of ethyl bromide to yield compound $C$. The total number of hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of compound $C$ is
questions.solution:
Compound $P$ ($C_6H_6O$) is phenol.

Nitration of phenol with dilute $HNO_3$ yields a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol. Ortho-nitrophenol (isomer $A$) is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, while para-nitrophenol (isomer $B$) is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

When para-nitrophenol ($B$) is treated with aqueous $NaOH$, it forms sodium para-nitrophenoxide. This phenoxide ion undergoes Williamson ether synthesis upon reaction with ethyl bromide ($CH_3CH_2Br$) to yield para-nitrophenetole (1-ethoxy-4-nitrobenzene) as compound $C$.

The structure of compound $C$ is $C_6H_4(NO_2)(OCH_2CH_3)$.

Counting the hydrogen atoms: there are 4 hydrogen atoms on the benzene ring and 5 hydrogen atoms in the ethyl group.

Total number of hydrogen atoms = $4 + 5 = 9$.

Answer: $9$
questions.explanation:
Compound $P$ ($C_6H_6O$) is phenol.

Nitration of phenol with dilute $HNO_3$ yields a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol. Ortho-nitrophenol (isomer $A$) is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, while para-nitrophenol (isomer $B$) is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

When para-nitrophenol ($B$) is treated with aqueous $NaOH$, it forms sodium para-nitrophenoxide. This phenoxide ion undergoes Williamson ether synthesis upon reaction with ethyl bromide ($CH_3CH_2Br$) to yield para-nitrophenetole (1-ethoxy-4-nitrobenzene) as compound $C$.

The structure of compound $C$ is $C_6H_4(NO_2)(OCH_2CH_3)$.

Counting the hydrogen atoms: there are 4 hydrogen atoms on the benzene ring and 5 hydrogen atoms in the ethyl group.

Total number of hydrogen atoms = $4 + 5 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

In the Carius method for the estimation of halogens, $250 \text{ mg}$ of an organic compound gave a certain mass of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ precipitate. If the percentage of bromine in the compound is $32\%$, the mass of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ formed is _______ mg.
(Given : molar mass in $\mathrm{g \ mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{Ag} : 108, \mathrm{Br} : 80$)
questions.question:
In the Carius method for the estimation of halogens, $250 \text{ mg}$ of an organic compound gave a certain mass of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ precipitate. If the percentage of bromine in the compound is $32\%$, the mass of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ formed is _______ mg.

Mass of bromine in the organic compound $= \dfrac{32}{100} \times 250 = 80 \text{ mg}$.

Moles of bromine $= \dfrac{80 \times 10^{-3}}{80} = 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$.

In the Carius method, 1 mole of $\mathrm{Br}$ produces 1 mole of $\mathrm{AgBr}$.

Moles of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ formed $= 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$.

Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Mass of $\mathrm{AgBr} = 10^{-3} \text{ mol} \times 188 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.188 \text{ g} = 188 \text{ mg}$.

Answer: $188$

questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound whose common name is $\beta$-ethoxy-$\alpha$-methylbutyraldehyde?
questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound whose common name is $\beta$-ethoxy-$\alpha$-methylbutyraldehyde?
questions.solution:
The common name is $\beta$-ethoxy-$\alpha$-methylbutyraldehyde.

The root word "butyraldehyde" indicates a continuous chain of 4 carbon atoms terminating in an aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$).

In common nomenclature, the carbon adjacent to the aldehyde group is the $\alpha$-carbon (which corresponds to C2 in IUPAC numbering), and the next carbon is the $\beta$-carbon (C3 in IUPAC).

The name specifies a methyl group at the $\alpha$-position (C2) and an ethoxy group at the $\beta$-position (C3).

Constructing the structure gives: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO}$.

For the IUPAC name, we number the longest chain starting from the aldehyde carbon as C1. The substituents are an ethoxy group at C3 and a methyl group at C2. Arranging the substituents alphabetically, the IUPAC name is 3-ethoxy-2-methylbutanal.

Answer: 3-ethoxy-2-methylbutanal

questions.question: During the estimation of nitrogen in an organic compound using Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia gas evolved from $1.4\text{ g}$ of the compound is passed into $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The residual acid requires $80\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M NaOH}$ for complete neutralization. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is _____ .
questions.solution:
The total milliequivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ initially taken:
$\text{meq}_{\text{initial}} = \text{Volume} \times \text{Molarity} \times \text{n-factor}$
$\text{meq}_{\text{initial}} = 100 \times 0.5 \times 2 = 100\text{ meq}$

The milliequivalents of $\text{NaOH}$ used for back-titration:
$\text{meq}_{\text{NaOH}} = 80 \times 0.5 \times 1 = 40\text{ meq}$

The milliequivalents of acid consumed by the evolved ammonia:
$\text{meq}_{\text{consumed}} = 100 - 40 = 60\text{ meq}$

The percentage of nitrogen is calculated as:
$\%\text{N} = \dfrac{1.4 \times \text{meq}_{\text{consumed}}}{w}$

Substituting the values:
$\%\text{N} = \dfrac{1.4 \times 60}{1.4} = 60$

Answer: $60$

The correct decreasing order of acidity for the most acidic hydrogen atom in the following compounds is:
(I) 1,3-cyclopentadiene
(II) 1-butyne
(III) 1-butene
(IV) butane
questions.question:
The correct decreasing order of acidity for the most acidic hydrogen atom in the following compounds is:
(I) 1,3-cyclopentadiene
(II) 1-butyne
(III) 1-butene
(IV) butane
questions.solution:
Acidity is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base formed after the removal of a proton ($H^+$).

For (I) 1,3-cyclopentadiene, the removal of a proton from the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon yields the cyclopentadienyl anion. This anion is planar, cyclic, completely conjugated, and has $6\pi$ electrons, making it aromatic and exceptionally stable.

For (II) 1-butyne, the terminal hydrogen is attached to an $sp$ hybridized carbon (50\% s-character), making the resulting carbanion relatively stable due to the high electronegativity of the $sp$ carbon.

For (III) 1-butene, the most acidic vinylic hydrogen is on an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon (33.3\% s-character).

For (IV) butane, the hydrogen is on an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon (25\% s-character), forming the least stable carbanion.

Therefore, the decreasing order of conjugate base stability, and hence acidity, is (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV).

Answer: (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV)

questions.question:
What is the correct IUPAC name of the following compound?

$\mathrm{Cl-CH_2-CH_2-CH=CH-CH(Br)-CH_3}$
questions.solution:
The parent chain is a 6-carbon alkene (hexene).

The double bond is at C3 from both ends.

Numbering from left-to-right gives substituents at C1 (chloro) and C5 (bromo), resulting in the locant set {1, 5}.

Numbering from right-to-left gives substituents at C2 (bromo) and C6 (chloro), resulting in the locant set {2, 6}.

According to the lowest locant rule, the set {1, 5} is preferred over {2, 6} because the first point of difference gives a lower number (1 < 2). Thus, left-to-right numbering is correct.

Finally, the substituents are arranged in alphabetical order: 'bromo' comes before 'chloro'.

The correct IUPAC name is 5-Bromo-1-chlorohex-3-ene.

Answer: 5-Bromo-1-chlorohex-3-ene

When a certain mass of this compound is analysed using Duma's method, it yields $24.6\text{ mL}$ of nitrogen gas collected over water at $300\text{ K}$ and $775\text{ mmHg}$ pressure. questions.question:
An organic compound is known to contain $20\%$ nitrogen by mass. When a certain mass of this compound is analysed using Duma's method, it yields $24.6\text{ mL}$ of nitrogen gas collected over water at $300\text{ K}$ and $775\text{ mmHg}$ pressure. The mass of the organic compound taken for the analysis is ________ $\text{mg}$.

(Given: Aqueous tension at $300\text{ K}$ is $15\text{ mmHg}$, $R = 0.082\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Pressure of dry $\text{N}_{2}$ gas $= P_{\text{total}} - \text{Aqueous tension}$
$P = 775 - 15 = 760\text{ mmHg} = 1\text{ atm}$

Using the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$
$1 \times 0.0246 = n \times 0.082 \times 300$
$n = \dfrac{0.0246}{24.6} = 0.001\text{ mol}$

Mass of nitrogen gas $= 0.001 \times 28 = 0.028\text{ g}$

Let the mass of the organic compound be $m$.
Percentage of nitrogen $= \dfrac{\text{Mass of N}}{\text{Mass of compound}} \times 100$
$20 = \dfrac{0.028}{m} \times 100$
$m = \dfrac{2.8}{20} = 0.14\text{ g}$

Mass in mg $= 0.14 \times 1000 = 140\text{ mg}$.

Answer: $140$

Consider the following hydrocarbons:
(I) 1,3-Cyclopentadiene
(II) Cyclopropene
(III) Cyclopentane
(IV) 1,4-Pentadiene

The correct decreasing order of their $\mathrm{pK_a}$ values (considering the most acidic $\mathrm{sp^3}$ $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond) is:
questions.question:
Consider the following hydrocarbons:
(I) 1,3-Cyclopentadiene
(II) Cyclopropene
(III) Cyclopentane
(IV) 1,4-Pentadiene

The correct decreasing order of their $\mathrm{pK_a}$ values (considering the most acidic $\mathrm{sp^3}$ $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond) is:
questions.solution:
The acidic strength of a hydrocarbon depends on the stability of its conjugate base (carbanion). A more stable conjugate base implies a stronger acid and a lower $\mathrm{pK_a}$ value.

Deprotonation of the most acidic $\mathrm{sp^3}$ $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond yields the following carbanions:
(I) 1,3-Cyclopentadiene gives the cyclopentadienyl anion, which is aromatic ($6\pi$ electrons) and highly stable.
(II) Cyclopropene gives the cyclopropenyl anion, which is anti-aromatic ($4\pi$ electrons) and highly unstable.
(III) Cyclopentane gives the cyclopentyl anion, which is a localized, non-aromatic carbanion.
(IV) 1,4-Pentadiene gives the pentadienyl anion, which is stabilized by resonance (delocalized over two double bonds) but is non-aromatic.

The stability order of these carbanions is: (I) > (IV) > (III) > (II).
Consequently, the acidic strength order is: (I) > (IV) > (III) > (II).
Since $\mathrm{pK_a}$ is inversely proportional to acidic strength, the decreasing order of $\mathrm{pK_a}$ values is: (II) > (III) > (IV) > (I).

Answer: (II) > (III) > (IV) > (I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider a planar, completely conjugated monocyclic hydrocarbon monocation containing $n$ carbon atoms. If this species is aromatic according to Hückel's rule, which of the following is a possible value for $n$?
questions.question: Consider a planar, completely conjugated monocyclic hydrocarbon monocation containing $n$ carbon atoms. If this species is aromatic according to Hückel's rule, which of the following is a possible value for $n$?
questions.solution:
For a completely conjugated monocyclic hydrocarbon monocation with $n$ carbon atoms, one carbon atom bears a positive charge (contributing $0$ $\pi$-electrons) and the remaining $(n-1)$ carbon atoms participate in $\pi$-bonding.

Thus, the total number of $\pi$-electrons is $(n-1)$.

According to Hückel's rule, for the species to be aromatic, the number of $\pi$-electrons must be equal to $(4k + 2)$, where $k$ is a non-negative integer ($k = 0, 1, 2, \dots$).

Equating the two:
$n - 1 = 4k + 2$
$n = 4k + 3$

Checking the given options:
If $k = 1$, $n = 4(1) + 3 = 7$.

Therefore, $n = 7$ is a valid number of carbon atoms for such an aromatic monocation (e.g., the tropylium cation).

Answer: $7$

questions.q:
An organic liquid is purified by steam distillation. The distillation is carried out at a temperature where the total atmospheric pressure is $760$ mm Hg. The vapour pressure of water at this distillation temperature is $700$ mm Hg. If the distillate contains $1.5$ g of the organic liquid and $1.8$ g of water, the molar mass of the organic liquid is:
(Given: Molar mass of water is $18$ g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.question:
An organic liquid is purified by steam distillation. The distillation is carried out at a temperature where the total atmospheric pressure is $760$ mm Hg. The vapour pressure of water at this distillation temperature is $700$ mm Hg. If the distillate contains $1.5$ g of the organic liquid and $1.8$ g of water, the molar mass of the organic liquid is:
(Given: Molar mass of water is $18$ g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
In steam distillation, the total pressure is the sum of the partial vapour pressures of the organic liquid ($P_l$) and water ($P_w$).
$P_{total} = P_l + P_w$
$760 = P_l + 700$
$P_l = 60$ mm Hg

The ratio of the masses of the organic liquid ($w_l$) and water ($w_w$) in the distillate is related to their partial pressures and molar masses by the equation:
$\dfrac{w_l}{w_w} = \dfrac{P_l M_l}{P_w M_w}$
where $M_l$ and $M_w$ are the molar masses of the organic liquid and water, respectively.

Substituting the given values:
$\dfrac{1.5}{1.8} = \dfrac{60 \times M_l}{700 \times 18}$
$\dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{60 \times M_l}{12600}$
$M_l = \dfrac{5 \times 12600}{6 \times 60} = \dfrac{5 \times 210}{6} = 5 \times 35 = 175$ g mol$^{-1}$.

Answer: $175$ g mol$^{-1}$

An organic compound 'Z' exhibits the following properties:
(i) It gives effervescence with aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution.
(ii) It contains exactly one chiral carbon atom.
(iii) It contains exactly one $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atom and exactly two $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized carbon atoms.

Identify the correct structure of Compound 'Z' from the given options.
questions.question:
An organic compound 'Z' exhibits the following properties:
(i) It gives effervescence with aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution.
(ii) It contains exactly one chiral carbon atom.
(iii) It contains exactly one $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atom and exactly two $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized carbon atoms.

Identify the correct structure of Compound 'Z' from the given options.
questions.solution:
Property (i) indicates the presence of a strongly acidic group like a carboxylic acid ($-\mathrm{COOH}$) group, which gives effervescence with aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$.
Property (ii) requires exactly one chiral center (an $\mathrm{sp^3}$ carbon attached to four different groups).
Property (iii) requires exactly one $\mathrm{sp^2}$ carbon and two $\mathrm{sp}$ carbons.

Evaluating the options:
Option 1: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-C \equiv C-COOH}$ has no chiral carbon.
Option 2: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-C \equiv C-CH_2OH}$ lacks a $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group (no effervescence with $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$) and has zero $\mathrm{sp^2}$ carbons.
Option 3: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CH=CH-COOH}$ has three $\mathrm{sp^2}$ carbons and zero $\mathrm{sp}$ carbons.
Option 4: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-C \equiv C-COOH}$ has a $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group, one chiral carbon ($\mathrm{-CH(NH_2)-}$), one $\mathrm{sp^2}$ carbon (in $-\mathrm{COOH}$), and two $\mathrm{sp}$ carbons (in $-\mathrm{C \equiv C}-$). Thus, it satisfies all criteria.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-C \equiv C-COOH}$

Molar ratio of $\text{C} : \text{H} : \text{N} = 0.02 : 0.02 : 0.002 = 10 : 10 : 1$

The empirical formula is $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{10}\text{N}$.
Thus, $x = 10$, $y = 10$, $z = 1$.
Value of $(x + y + z) = 10 + 10 + 1 = 21$.

Answer: $21$

Thus, $x = 10$, $y = 10$, $z = 1$.

Answer: $21$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The isobutyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_2CH-\overset{+}{C}H_2$, undergoes a spontaneous 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable carbocation. What is the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens present in the initial carbocation and in the newly formed rearranged carbocation, respectively?
questions.question: The isobutyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_2CH-\overset{+}{C}H_2$, undergoes a spontaneous 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable carbocation. What is the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens present in the initial carbocation and in the newly formed rearranged carbocation, respectively?
questions.solution:
The number of $\alpha$-hydrogens is determined by counting the hydrogen atoms attached to the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms directly adjacent to the positively charged carbon.

In the initial isobutyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_2CH-\overset{+}{C}H_2$, the positively charged carbon is attached to only one adjacent carbon (the CH group). This adjacent carbon has exactly 1 hydrogen atom. Thus, there is $1$ $\alpha$-hydrogen.

The initial primary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift, moving the hydrogen from the adjacent tertiary carbon to the primary carbon. This rearrangement forms the tert-butyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_3C^+$.

In the rearranged tert-butyl carbocation, the positively charged carbon is attached to three methyl ($-CH_3$) groups. Each methyl group has 3 hydrogen atoms, giving a total of $3 \times 3 = 9$ $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Therefore, the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens in the initial and rearranged carbocations are $1$ and $9$, respectively.

Answer: $1$ and $9$

Reaction 1: Excess $\text{NaHCO}_3$
Reaction 2: Excess $\text{NaOH}$
Reaction 3: Excess $\text{NaNH}_2$

Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be the number of moles of acidic protons neutralized per mole of the compound in Reaction 1, Reaction 2, and Reaction 3, respectively.
The values of $x$, $y$, and $z$ are:
questions.question:
One mole of 4-ethynyl-3-hydroxybenzoic acid is treated separately with excess amounts of three different bases in three separate reactions:
Reaction 1: Excess $\text{NaHCO}_3$
Reaction 2: Excess $\text{NaOH}$
Reaction 3: Excess $\text{NaNH}_2$

Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be the number of moles of acidic protons neutralized per mole of the compound in Reaction 1, Reaction 2, and Reaction 3, respectively.
The values of $x$, $y$, and $z$ are:
questions.solution:
The given molecule, 4-ethynyl-3-hydroxybenzoic acid, contains three distinct acidic functional groups:
1. A carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$), $\text{p}K_a \approx 4$
2. A phenolic hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$), $\text{p}K_a \approx 10$
3. A terminal alkyne group ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$), $\text{p}K_a \approx 25$

An acid-base reaction proceeds in the forward direction if the reacting base is stronger than the conjugate base of the acid (i.e., the conjugate acid of the base must have a higher $\text{p}K_a$ than the acid being deprotonated).

Reaction 1: $\text{NaHCO}_3$ is a weak base (conjugate acid $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$, $\text{p}K_a \approx 6.4$). It is strong enough to deprotonate only the $-\text{COOH}$ group. Thus, $x = 1$.

Reaction 2: $\text{NaOH}$ is a moderately strong base (conjugate acid $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{p}K_a \approx 15.7$). It can deprotonate both the $-\text{COOH}$ and the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ groups, but it is not strong enough to deprotonate the terminal alkyne. Thus, $y = 2$.

Reaction 3: $\text{NaNH}_2$ is a very strong base (conjugate acid $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{p}K_a \approx 38$). It is strong enough to deprotonate all three acidic groups: $-\text{COOH}$, phenolic $-\text{OH}$, and the terminal alkyne. Thus, $z = 3$.

The correct values are $x = 1$, $y = 2$, and $z = 3$.

Answer: $x = 1$, $y = 2$, $z = 3$

An organic compound is known to contain $50.8\%$ of iodine by mass. When a sample of this compound is subjected to the Carius method for the estimation of halogens, it yields $0.47 \text{ g}$ of silver iodide $(\text{AgI})$ precipitate. The mass of the original organic compound sample taken for the analysis is $\ldots\ldots \text{ mg}$.
(Given: Atomic masses of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ u}$ and $\text{I} = 127 \text{ u}$)
questions.question:
An organic compound is known to contain $50.8\%$ of iodine by mass. When a sample of this compound is subjected to the Carius method for the estimation of halogens, it yields $0.47 \text{ g}$ of silver iodide $(\text{AgI})$ precipitate. The mass of the original organic compound sample taken for the analysis is $\ldots\ldots \text{ mg}$.
(Given: Atomic masses of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ u}$ and $\text{I} = 127 \text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{AgI} = 108 + 127 = 235 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of $\text{AgI}$ formed $= \dfrac{0.47}{235} = 0.002 \text{ mol}$

Moles of iodine in the sample $= \text{Moles of AgI} = 0.002 \text{ mol}$

Mass of iodine $= 0.002 \times 127 = 0.254 \text{ g}$

Let the mass of the organic compound be $W \text{ g}$.

Percentage of iodine $= \left( \dfrac{\text{Mass of iodine}}{W} \right) \times 100$

$50.8 = \dfrac{0.254}{W} \times 100$

$W = \dfrac{25.4}{50.8} = 0.5 \text{ g}$

Mass in mg $= 0.5 \times 1000 = 500 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $500$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of their basic strength:

(I) $4$-nitroaniline
(II) $3$-nitroaniline
(III) $3$-methoxyaniline
(IV) $4$-methoxyaniline
questions.question:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of their basic strength:

(I) $4$-nitroaniline
(II) $3$-nitroaniline
(III) $3$-methoxyaniline
(IV) $4$-methoxyaniline
questions.solution:
Basic strength of anilines depends on the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation. Electron donating groups (EDG) increase basicity, while electron withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease it.

In (IV) $4$-methoxyaniline, the $-OCH_3$ group is at the para position. It exerts a strong $+M$ effect which dominates over its $-I$ effect, increasing the electron density on the nitrogen atom and making it the most basic.

In (III) $3$-methoxyaniline, the $-OCH_3$ group is at the meta position where the mesomeric effect does not operate. It exerts only a $-I$ effect, which mildly decreases the basicity.

In (II) $3$-nitroaniline, the $-NO_2$ group is at the meta position and exerts a strong $-I$ effect. Since the $-I$ effect of $-NO_2$ is stronger than that of $-OCH_3$, (II) is less basic than (III).

In (I) $4$-nitroaniline, the $-NO_2$ group is at the para position. It exerts both strong $-M$ and $-I$ effects, drastically reducing the electron density on the nitrogen atom and making it the least basic.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of basic strength is (IV) > (III) > (II) > (I).

Answer: (IV) > (III) > (II) > (I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider a compound with a six-membered carbon ring containing one double bond. A hydroxyl ($-OH$) group is attached to an allylic carbon. A methyl group is attached to the ring such that, moving along the saturated carbons away from the double bond, it is on the second carbon after the $-OH$ bearing carbon. What is the correct IUPAC name of this compound?
questions.question: Consider a compound with a six-membered carbon ring containing one double bond. A hydroxyl ($-OH$) group is attached to an allylic carbon. A methyl group is attached to the ring such that, moving along the saturated carbons away from the double bond, it is on the second carbon after the $-OH$ bearing carbon. What is the correct IUPAC name of this compound?
questions.solution:
The principal functional group is the hydroxyl group ($-OH$), so the carbon bearing it is assigned locant 1.

The ring must be numbered to give the double bond the lowest possible locant. Numbering towards the double bond gives it locant 2 (positions 2 and 3). Numbering in the opposite direction (away from the double bond) would give it locant 5.

Therefore, we number towards the double bond: C1 has the $-OH$ group, and C2=C3 is the double bond. Continuing around the ring, C4 is a $-CH_2-$ group, and C5 bears the methyl group (which matches the description of being the second carbon after C1 along the saturated path).

The substituent is a methyl group at position 5. The principal functional group is an alcohol at position 1, and the double bond is at position 2.

Combining these parts gives the correct IUPAC name: 5-Methylcyclohex-2-en-1-ol.

Answer: 5-Methylcyclohex-2-en-1-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the following isomeric carbocations that can theoretically form as intermediates during the electrophilic addition of $H^+$ to 1-methoxybuta-1,3-diene. Which of these carbocations is the most thermodynamically stable?
questions.question: Consider the following isomeric carbocations that can theoretically form as intermediates during the electrophilic addition of $H^+$ to 1-methoxybuta-1,3-diene. Which of these carbocations is the most thermodynamically stable?
questions.solution:
The stability of a carbocation is determined by the extent of delocalization of the positive charge and the ability of substituents to donate electron density.

Let us analyze the given carbocations:
- $CH_3-O-CH=CH-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3$: This is an allylic carbocation. The positive charge can delocalize via resonance to the carbon adjacent to the oxygen atom ($CH_3-O-\overset{+}{C}H-CH=CH-CH_3$). The oxygen atom then donates its lone pair through a strong $+M$ effect, creating a resonance structure where all atoms have complete octets. This ion benefits from both extended conjugation and octet completion.
- $CH_3-O-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_2-CH=CH_2$: The positive charge is directly adjacent to the oxygen atom, receiving $+M$ stabilization and forming a complete octet. However, the positive charge is isolated from the alkene double bond by an $sp^3$ hybridized $-CH_2-$ group, so it lacks extended allylic conjugation.
- $CH_3-O-CH_2-\overset{+}{C}H-CH=CH_2$: This is an allylic carbocation, but the positive charge cannot delocalize to the carbon adjacent to the oxygen due to the intervening $sp^3$ carbon. It only receives stabilization from the alkene and weak inductive effects.
- $CH_3-O-CH=CH-CH_2-\overset{+}{C}H_2$: This is a primary carbocation with no resonance stabilization from the double bond or the oxygen atom.

Because $CH_3-O-CH=CH-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3$ achieves a complete-octet resonance structure while also benefiting from extended conjugation across the carbon skeleton, it is the most thermodynamically stable intermediate.

Answer: $CH_3-O-CH=CH-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3$

questions.q: In Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen, $0.5\text{ g}$ of an organic compound was digested and the evolved ammonia was completely neutralized by a solution of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$. If the percentage of nitrogen in the given organic compound is $42\%$, the volume of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ required is _______ $\text{mL}$.
questions.question: In Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen, $0.5\text{ g}$ of an organic compound was digested and the evolved ammonia was completely neutralized by a solution of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$. If the percentage of nitrogen in the given organic compound is $42\%$, the volume of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ required is _______ $\text{mL}$.
questions.solution:
The formula for the percentage of nitrogen in Kjeldahl's method is given by:

$\% \text{N} = \dfrac{1.4 \times N_{\text{acid}} \times V_{\text{acid}}}{W}$

where $N_{\text{acid}}$ is the normality of the acid, $V_{\text{acid}}$ is the volume of the acid in $\text{mL}$, and $W$ is the mass of the organic compound.

Given:
Mass of organic compound, $W = 0.5\text{ g}$
Percentage of nitrogen = $42\%$
Molarity of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 0.5\text{ M}$

The basicity (n-factor) of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $2$.
Normality of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $N_{\text{acid}} = \text{Molarity} \times 2 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1\text{ N}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$42 = \dfrac{1.4 \times 1 \times V_{\text{acid}}}{0.5}$

$42 \times 0.5 = 1.4 \times V_{\text{acid}}$

$21 = 1.4 \times V_{\text{acid}}$

$V_{\text{acid}} = \dfrac{21}{1.4} = 15\text{ mL}$

The volume of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ required is $15\text{ mL}$.

Answer: $15$

Normality of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $N_{\text{acid}} = \text{Molarity} \times 2 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1\text{ N}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$42 = \dfrac{1.4 \times 1 \times V_{\text{acid}}}{0.5}$

$42 \times 0.5 = 1.4 \times V_{\text{acid}}$

$21 = 1.4 \times V_{\text{acid}}$

$V_{\text{acid}} = \dfrac{21}{1.4} = 15\text{ mL}$

The volume of $0.5\text{ M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ required is $15\text{ mL}$.

Answer: $15$

Therefore, the correct IUPAC name is 2,7,8-Trimethyldecane.
