In a Carius estimation of bromine, an organic compound is found to contain $80\%$ bromine by mass. When $0.50\text{ g}$ of this compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate, the mass of silver bromide formed is $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{Br} = 80\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
In a Carius estimation of bromine, an organic compound is found to contain $80\%$ bromine by mass. When $0.50\text{ g}$ of this compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate, the mass of silver bromide formed is $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{Br} = 80\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The formula for the percentage of bromine in Carius estimation is:

$\% \text{ Br} = \dfrac{\text{Atomic mass of Br}}{\text{Molar mass of AgBr}} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of AgBr formed}}{\text{Mass of organic compound}} \times 100$

Given data:
$\% \text{ Br} = 80$
Mass of organic compound $= 0.50\text{ g}$
Molar mass of $\text{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188\text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$80 = \dfrac{80}{188} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of AgBr}}{0.50} \times 100$

Simplifying the equation:
$1 = \dfrac{1}{188} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of AgBr}}{0.50} \times 100$

$\text{Mass of AgBr} = \dfrac{188 \times 0.50}{100} = 0.94\text{ g}$

Expressing this in the required format:
$\text{Mass of AgBr} = 94 \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}$

Comparing with $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}$, we get $x = 94$.

Answer: $94$

questions.q:
The correct decreasing order of stability of the following carbanions is:

(I) Cyclopentadienyl anion
(II) $p$-Nitrobenzyl anion
(III) Benzyl anion
(IV) Cyclopropenyl anion
questions.question:
The correct decreasing order of stability of the following carbanions is:

(I) Cyclopentadienyl anion
(II) $p$-Nitrobenzyl anion
(III) Benzyl anion
(IV) Cyclopropenyl anion
questions.solution:
The stability of carbanions depends on factors like aromaticity, resonance, and inductive/mesomeric effects.

(I) Cyclopentadienyl anion is a planar, cyclic system with $6\pi$ electrons. It follows Huckel's rule and is aromatic, making it exceptionally stable.

(IV) Cyclopropenyl anion is a planar, cyclic system with $4\pi$ electrons. It is anti-aromatic and highly unstable.

(II) $p$-Nitrobenzyl anion and (III) Benzyl anion are both stabilized by resonance. However, in the $p$-nitrobenzyl anion, the $-\text{NO}_2$ group exerts strong $-\text{M}$ and $-\text{I}$ effects, which withdraw electron density and further stabilize the negative charge compared to the unsubstituted benzyl anion.

Following the general stability hierarchy (Aromatic $>$ Resonance with $-\text{M}$ $>$ Resonance $>$ Anti-aromatic), the correct decreasing order of stability is (I) $>$ (II) $>$ (III) $>$ (IV).

Answer: (I) $>$ (II) $>$ (III) $>$ (IV)

Higher acidity corresponds to a lower $pK_a$ value.

The correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

(B) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$
(C) $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OOC}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$
(D) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$

The correct decreasing order of $\text{p}K_a$ values for the most acidic protons in these compounds is:
questions.question:
Consider the following compounds:
(A) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$
(B) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$
(C) $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OOC}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$
(D) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$

The correct decreasing order of $\text{p}K_a$ values for the most acidic protons in these compounds is:
questions.solution:
The $\text{p}K_a$ value of an acid is inversely proportional to its acidic strength. A weaker acid has a higher $\text{p}K_a$ value.

The acidity of the given compounds depends on the stability of the carbanion formed after the removal of the most acidic proton. The stability of the carbanion is determined by the electron-withdrawing ability of the adjacent groups.

Compound (D) has only one carbonyl group, making its carbanion the least stable and the compound the least acidic (highest $\text{p}K_a$).

Compounds (A), (B), and (C) have active methylene groups flanked by two carbonyl-containing groups. The ester group ($-\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$) exhibits cross-conjugation, where the lone pair of the alkoxy oxygen donates electron density to the carbonyl carbon. This reduces the carbonyl group's ability to withdraw electron density from the carbanion compared to a ketone group ($-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$).

Therefore, the electron-withdrawing power follows the order: two ketones > one ketone and one ester > two esters.

The acidic strength order is: (A) > (B) > (C) > (D).

Consequently, the decreasing order of $\text{p}K_a$ values is the reverse: $D > C > B > A$.

Answer: $D > C > B > A$

questions.q: Which of the following cyclic ketones will form an oxime that exhibits geometrical isomerism upon reaction with hydroxylamine?
questions.question: Which of the following cyclic ketones will form an oxime that exhibits geometrical isomerism upon reaction with hydroxylamine?
questions.solution:
For an oxime ($>C=N-OH$) to exhibit geometrical isomerism, the two groups attached to the carbon atom of the $C=N$ bond must be different. In the case of cyclic ketones, this implies that the two paths around the ring starting from the carbonyl carbon must be non-identical.

Let us examine the given ketones:
1. 4-Ethylcyclohexanone: The paths from C1 to C4 are identical (symmetric with respect to the plane passing through C1 and C4). Thus, the oxime will not show geometrical isomerism.
2. 4,4-Dimethylcyclohexanone: Similar to 4-ethylcyclohexanone, it has a plane of symmetry passing through C1 and C4. The two paths around the ring are identical.
3. 3-Methylcyclohexanone: The paths from C1 to C3 are different (one path goes through a $CH_2$ group then a $CH(CH_3)$ group, while the other goes through three $CH_2$ groups). Because the two paths are non-identical, its oxime will exhibit geometrical isomerism (syn and anti forms).
4. Cyclohexanone: The ring is completely symmetrical, so the two paths are identical.

Therefore, 3-Methylcyclohexanone forms an oxime that exhibits geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 3-Methylcyclohexanone
